title: Windows Server 2025 gets support for quick machine recovery
content_md: Microsoft announced that IT administrators can now use quick machine recovery on Windows Server 2025 after installing the October 2026 security update. Quick machine recovery (QMR) lets IT admins fix critical boot failures with targeted Windows Update fixes without physical access to affected systems. When enabled, it boots into the Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE) and launches the QMR Tool if Windows 11 fails to start because of a configuration change or a new driver. It then sends crash data to Microsoft, which can remotely fix issues by adjusting settings or removing problematic drivers or updates. "With the October 2026 security update, quick machine recovery extends to Windows Server 2025," the company said in a message center update. "Quick machine recovery is designed to help restore devices experiencing widespread boot issues by using the Windows Recovery Environment (WinRE) to search Windows Update for applicable remediations." On Windows Server 2025, cloud remediation is disabled by default, but admins can enable it via Group Policy under Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > System > Quick Machine Recovery to retrieve and apply cloud-sourced remediation. For local configuration, admins must sign in to the target server with administrator permissions and use the Local Group Policy Editor.
